messages:
alex: Heads up — working on a fallback compatibility matrix for tiered routing. Need a quick sync on tokenizer/context/tool-call parity across variants. Pinging @mira @sam.
mira: Do we have an existing matrix? Last time we saw gaps around BPE vs sentencepiece shifting token counts which broke some tool-calling expectations.
sam: Yep. Tokenizer mismatches + differing max_context are the big ones. If we fallback to a lower-context variant we need a clear truncation policy + telemetry to quantify token loss.
jordan: Proposed quick schema (CSV-like):
```
model_variant,tokenizer,max_ctx,tool_call,kv_compat
redwood-13b,bpe,8192,yes,preserve
redwood-13b-q4,sentencepiece,4096,no,drop
```
mira: :thinking_face: Tool-calling parity is the nastiest. For Dedicated/comitted customers prefer seamless fallback (try preserve), otherwise return a clear fallback code so apps can decide to retry or show degrade.
alex: UX idea — Console rollout should show a per-route "fallback risk" score + tooltip. Also add widgets: %requests that fell back, % tool-calls lost.
deploy-bot: canary-rollout started for routing-policy v2 on us-west-2.
sam: Telemetry keys to add: fallback_reason=(tokenizer|context|toolcall|kv), orig_variant, fallback_variant, token_loss_estimate. Keep payload compact.
jordan: Also update SDKs: surface fallback headers and a safe field e.g. `x-rw-fallback-toolcall` so clients can detect preserved function-call state.
mira: :thumbsup: I'll draft the matrix and brief UX copy. alex can you own the console mocks? sam can hook the telemetry?
alex: Yup. I'll drop a tiny Figma mock + link in the next thread.
